thread:
Alex: Hey team — noticed a sharp spike in 5xx from /v1/generate in us-west-2 starting ~08:12 UTC. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% over ~5m. Customer error reports trickling in. Paging now :rotating_light:
Morgan: on it. I see the alert firing in Grafana. Heatmap shows tail latency climb then errors. Any recent deploys?
Alex: No deploys from our side. Autoscaler did a few restarts. Logs show some GPU memory allocation failures and a bunch of 'CUDA out of memory' traces.
OncallBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1795123456 — High error rate on inference service (us-west-2). Notifying on-call rotation.
PagerDuty: Paging on-call: @Morgan -> primary. Escalation in 5m.
Morgan: attaching a small grep output.
Morgan: ```
$ kubectl -n inference-prod logs inference-5f6b -c runtime | tail -n 60
2026-03-15T08:13:21Z runtime ERROR allocation failed: CUDA OOM on device 0
2026-03-15T08:13:22Z runtime INFO restarted worker 0
2026-03-15T08:13:23Z runtime ERROR model load timeout for shard 2
```
Sarah: I can check routing and cache hit rates — maybe KV cache thrashing after a model fallback?
Jordan: I'm looking at the model variants. We had a transient fallback to a larger fp16 model for a small subset of requests due to a routing mismatch. That would explain memory pressure.
Alex: Confirmed: smart-routing sent ~8% of traffic to model-x-large (still warmup) instead of model-x-quant. Setting route pins now.
Morgan: For mitigation, I've pinned route policy to prefer quantized variants and drained pods running large model. Doing a gradual restart to evict the big workers.
OncallBot: Event: Route override applied by Morgan at 08:20 UTC. Posting service events to thread.
Morgan: Errors are dropping — back to ~0.4% after the override. Still seeing noisy alerts from the old metric that fires on transient spikes.
Alex: Customer impact: a handful of requests failed for two enterprise tenants — CS flagged 3 incidents. We should do a brief customer impact assessment and push a note.
Sarah: Agreed. I'll assemble a short blameless note with timestamps and affected segments. Also suggest we schedule an alert-tuning postmortem to address false positives.
Jordan: Root cause draft: smart-routing allowed fallback to non-quantized model during a transient capacity mismatch; larger model caused GPU OOMs and pod restarts. Contributing factor: alert threshold for 5xx is too sensitive during autoscaler churn.
Alex: Action items for immediate follow-up: 1) Update routing policy to enforce prefer-quantized for that model family (Jordan) 2) Add short cooldown to 5xx alert to reduce paging on short spikes (Morgan + eng-sre) 3) Create a dashboard showing per-model memory pressure and routing decisions (Sarah) 4) Customer comms draft (Alex)
Morgan: For the alert cooldown I'm proposing: change rule from 'IF 5xx_rate > 1% for 2m' to 'IF 5xx_rate > 1% for 5m OR sustained error spike aligned with pod restarts'. That will turn many of the immediate pages into tickets and reduce noise.
Jordan: We should avoid masking real Sev1 incidents. Let's map routing: Sev1 (service-down or high user-impact) -> page eng-oncall + eng-sre; Sev2 (partial degradation, sustained) -> page eng-oncall; Sev3 (short spikes / low impact) -> ticket eng-sre. Also include model fallback events as a signal to escalate faster.
Alex: +1. Also add runbook pointer to the alert text so recipients can triage faster (link to /docs/runbooks/oom-model-fallback).
Sarah: I'll create the dashboard and a new panel that correlates route choice, model size, and GPU memory used per pod. That should help tune thresholds. ETA end of day.
Morgan: I'll open a ticket to change the alert group/route: add a 3m fire window before pager for 5xx, and create a separate immediate pager for 'pod restart rate > 3 in 5m' which indicates instability.
OncallBot: Action created: TICKET-3478 (alert tuning) assigned to Morgan.
Alex: Customer comms draft sent to #customer-notify for approval. No SLA breach expected but offer mitigations.
Jordan: Postmortem plan: 1) timeline & impact 2) root cause 3) why routing chose the large model 4) alert tuning + dashboard 5) config change to prevent fallback to large models during autoscaler events. Volunteers: Jordan (root cause + routing), Sarah (dashboards), Morgan (alerts), Alex (comm/summary).
Sarah: I'll also add a Grafana alert that watches 'cache hit ratio < 60% and increased model loads' as early warning so routing can be considered before memory pressure spikes.
Morgan: Putting a temporary suppression on the noisy 5xx pager for the next 30m while we watch. Will revert if anything else looks off.
Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll treat this as Sev2 for now. Follow-ups tracked in TICKET-3478 and the postmortem doc. If impact grows, escalate to Sev1.
Jordan: Noted. I'll follow up with a proposed severity mapping doc for the on-call handbook — suggest changes to escalation windows and channel mappings.
Sarah: Quick note: update internal runbook to call out 'prefer-quantized' pin as a mitigation step; saved me ~10min triage time today.
PagerDuty: Incident INC-2026-1795123456 acknowledged by Morgan at 08:22 UTC.
Morgan: monitoring for 30m and will hand off to next on-call at 09:00 UTC. Handoff note: watch for recurring fallbacks and pod restart counts.
Alex: Handoff received. I'll take follow-ups for customer comms. Put handoff summary in the rotation.
OncallBot: Handoff logged: Morgan -> Alex at 08:58 UTC.
Sarah: Adding retrospective agenda item: 'reduce alert noise without losing signal' — want input from eng-sre and runtime teams.
Alex: Great. Closing thread for now; will update with the postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
